requirements.text: create a new HR service called End-to-End New Hire Lifecycle with fulfilment type as workflow, using the existing topic detail New Hire Onboarding and the New Hire Provisioning Template
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_service WHERE hr_service_id = 55 AND service_name = 'End-to-End New Hire Lifecycle' AND fulfillment_type = 'workflow' AND topic_detail = 24 AND service_template = 4 AND active = 1
requirements.source: Verify the new HR service exists, active, and linked
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_service_id is 54)
topic detail New Hire Onboarding is topic_detail 24, not the HR service of the same name (hr_service 11); New Hire Provisioning Template is service_template 4
active = 1 kept from the benchmark check; the pilot case must reference an active service (policy 3.1)

requirements.text: For that template, include the following: { "journey_code": "new_hire_standard", "auto_generate_tasks": true, "tasks": [...] }

change_request_values: (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.template')) FROM json_each(change_request_values, '$.tasks') AS t WHERE (json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.template') = 'HRT0001023' AND json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.step') = 1) OR (json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.template') = 'HRT0001025' AND json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.step') = 2) OR (json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.template') = 'HRT0001022' AND json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.step') = 3)) = 3

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_template WHERE service_template_id = 4 AND json_extract(change_request_values, '$.journey_code') = 'new_hire_standard' AND json_extract(change_request_values, '$.auto_generate_tasks') = 1 AND (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.template')) FROM json_each(change_request_values, '$.tasks') AS t WHERE (json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.template') = 'HRT0001023' AND json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.step') = 1) OR (json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.template') = 'HRT0001025' AND json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.step') = 2) OR (json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.template') = 'HRT0001022' AND json_extract(change_request_values, t.fullkey || '.step') = 3)) = 3
requirements.source: Verify the service template change request values were updated
assumptions: the request's JSON lacks the closing bracket of the tasks list; read as a three-element tasks list
each template is tested with the step the request pairs it with (HRT0001023 step 1, HRT0001025 step 2, HRT0001022 step 3); the benchmark check tests the template codes alone
auto_generate_tasks true is stored as JSON true, which json_extract reads as 1
the seed stores this column as a JSON object; keys the request does not name (notify_manager, sla_days) are not tested

requirements.text: retire the HR services Setup New Hire HR Profile and New Hire Documentation

requirements.source: Verify the two HR services were retired
assumptions: Setup New Hire HR Profile is hr_service 47 and New Hire Documentation is hr_service 10, both active on the seed
retire read as active = 0, the only status column on hr_service

requirements.text: retire the HR services Setup New Hire HR Profile and New Hire Documentation
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_service WHERE hr_service_id = 11 AND active = 1
assumptions: boundary of the retirement: the New Hire Onboarding service (hr_service 11) shares its name with the new service's topic detail, and 'shift everything to a single lifecycle service' could sweep it in, but the request retires only the two services it names

requirements.text: update the New Hire criteria so its users list includes thomas.green@servicenow.com and anne.medina@servicenow.com
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_criteria WHERE hr_criteria_id = 5 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(users) WHERE value = 1) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(users) WHERE value = 29)
requirements.source: Verify New Hire criteria users list includes Thomas + Anne
assumptions: New Hire criteria is hr_criteria 5; its users list is NULL on the seed
thomas.green@servicenow.com is user 1 (inactive on the seed) and anne.medina@servicenow.com is user 29
users stored as a JSON array of user ids: kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy, and no seed row holds a users list
'includes' allows other users in the list

disagreement: users: A tested only that the list was set (users IS NOT NULL), B tested that it holds user ids 1 and 29; chose the membership test because it is the benchmark check's own cell, nothing in the request, policy or seed contradicts the id form, and it is the tighter predicate

requirements.text: Make sure the Employee Onboarding skill is assigned to those same users
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_skill WHERE skill = 2 AND "user" = 1
requirements.source: Verify “Employee Onboarding” skill assigned to Thomas + Anne
assumptions: Employee Onboarding is skill 2; thomas.green@servicenow.com is user 1, who lacks it on the seed
two user_skill rows are created, so each is selected by skill and user rather than by id
user 1 is inactive on the seed; the policy sets no rule against giving an inactive user a skill

requirements.source: Verify “Employee Onboarding” skill assigned to Thomas + Anne

requirements.text: create a pilot case for employee tabitha.bullock@servicenow.com (account number: ACCT-PILOT, type: other), using the new lifecycle service with priority high, and coe type of Talent Management. Assign it to the HR Service Desk group and to anne.medina@servicenow.com
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 55 AND opened_for = 3 AND priority = 'high' AND coe_type = 'Talent Management' AND account_number = 'ACCT-PILOT' AND account_type = 'other' AND assignment_group = 4 AND assigned_to = 29
requirements.source: Verify the pilot case exists with correct service, priority, group, and assignee
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_id is 60)
hr_service 55 is the new lifecycle service created above
opened_for holds an hr_profile id; tabitha.bullock@servicenow.com is user 3 with hr_profile 3, so opened_for is 3 under either reading
HR Service Desk is user_group 4; anne.medina@servicenow.com is user 29
status and opened_by are not fixed by the request and are not tested

disagreement: skills: A skills IS NOT NULL, B untested; chose untested because hr_case.skills is a JSON column that is NULL on all 60 seed cases, so its storage format is not shown, and no benchmark check tests it

requirements.text: link the New Hire Orientation knowledge article to the case as suggested
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case_knowledge WHERE hr_case_kb_id = 13 AND hr_case_id = 61 AND knowledge_id = 2 AND used_as = 'suggested'
requirements.source: Verify KB “New Hire Orientation” linked as suggested
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_kb_id is 12)
New Hire Orientation is knowledge 2 (KB0040001), published and internal, so linkable under policy 4.2
the case is the pilot case, hr_case 61

notes:
disagreement: value: the New Hire criteria users cell: one pass tests only that the list was set, the other that it holds user ids 1 and 29 as the benchmark check does; kept the membership test, since it is the benchmark's own cell and nothing in the request, policy or seed contradicts the id form (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: disposition: 'Verify New Hire criteria users list includes Thomas + Anne': one pass repaired it by dropping the membership test as untestable, the other kept it; kept, because the benchmark check is the prior and the seed, though it holds no users list, does not contradict its user-id form.
disagreement: value: the pilot case's skills cell: one pass tests skills IS NOT NULL, the other leaves it out; left out, because hr_case.skills is a JSON column that is NULL on every seed case, so its storage format is not shown, and no benchmark check tests it (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: missing requirement: the Employee Onboarding skill: one pass carries both users in one requirement (skill 2 for users 1 and 29, count 2), the other has one requirement per user; kept one per user, since two rows are created in user_skill and each is selected by its natural key; both carry the benchmark's skill check.
The passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition; their texts and assumptions differ in wording only. The service template cells were written in two equivalent forms; the form keyed by the change_request_values column is kept, since cells are keyed by column.
Untestable: the case's skills (Employee Onboarding, skill 2) go in hr_case.skills, whose JSON format no seed case shows. The criteria users list is NULL on every seed row; it is tested as user ids, as the benchmark check assumes.
Policy conflicts carried as the request states them, consistent with the benchmark checks: the acting user Karen Watkins (user 39) has the admin role, and the policy says an administrator must not perform routine HR case work, yet the request has her create the pilot case and link the article; anne.medina@servicenow.com (user 29) belongs only to group 7, not HR Service Desk (group 4, members 15 and 22), while policy 3.2 requires the assignee to be a current member of the assignment group, and no listed tool adds a group membership; thomas.green@servicenow.com (user 1) is inactive, and the policy asks that a user's active status be validated before an operation.
The policy's default case state 'new' has no counterpart among the seed's case status values, so status is left to the server. The policy's short-description template and 30 to 120 character limit are a format rule the benchmark does not test and are left out. The request's JSON lacks the closing bracket of the tasks list and is read as three tasks.
